html:
Khartoum, the capital of Sudan, was founded in the 1820s as an Egyptian army camp where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet, and grew into the seat of government under Egyptian rule.

The Mahdists took and sacked it in the siege of 1885 and built their capital across the river at Omdurman. The British rebuilt Khartoum after 1898 with a street plan said to follow the British flag, and Gordon Memorial College, later the University of Khartoum.

With Omdurman and Khartoum North it formed one of the largest cities in Africa. In the war that began in 2023, fighting wrecked much of the city and most of its people fled. It stands at the heart of the Nile valley.
sum: Khartoum, the capital of Sudan, was founded in the 1820s as an Egyptian army camp where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet, and grew into the seat of government under Egyptian rule.
